source: Miyake et al. (2000) The unity and diversity of executive functions and their contributions to complex frontal lobe tasks
finding: Shifting, updating and inhibition are moderately correlated but separable. Each predicts different complex tasks.
numbers: N=137 college students. WCST tied most to Shifting, Tower of Hanoi to Inhibition, random number generation to Inhibition+Updating, operation span to Updating. Dual-task unrelated to all three.
limits: One student sample; latent factors depend on task choice; abstract read, not full paper.
agent_relevance: Treat control as several parts. S6 switching and holding state in context are different skills, so test them separately.

source: Friedman & Miyake (2017) Unity and diversity of executive functions: individual differences as a window on cognitive structure
finding: Later work shows inhibition has no unique variance: Common EF absorbs all correlation among inhibition tasks. Only Updating-Specific and Shifting-Specific remain.
numbers: Miyake 2000: task r from -.05 to .34; latent r .42 to .63. Twin data age 17: Common EF 96% heritable, Updating-Specific 100%, Shifting-Specific 79%. Updating-Specific r=.49 with IQ; Shifting-Specific r=-.24. Stability age 17 to 23: .86 / 1.0 / .91.
quote: Inhibiting factor is isomorphic with Common EF
limits: First 100k of 205k characters read. Authors say task impurity and low reliability depress task-level correlations.
agent_relevance: Inhibition as one trait is weak. Build agent checks for goal maintenance and for switching, not a generic ignore-distractions step.

source: Eysenck, Derakshan, Santos & Calvo (2007) Anxiety and cognitive performance: attentional control theory
finding: ACT: anxiety weakens the goal-directed attention system and strengthens the stimulus-driven one. Costs fall on inhibition and shifting. Compensatory effort can protect accuracy while efficiency drops.
numbers: Theory paper; no single effect size. Prediction: efficiency (RT, effort) hit more than effectiveness (accuracy).
limits: Abstract read only. Updating was added later (Eysenck and Derakshan 2011).
agent_relevance: Pressure framing in a prompt may act like anxiety: cost shows first as extra tokens and effort, then as errors.

source: Shi, Sharpe & Abbott (2019) A meta-analysis of the relationship between anxiety and attentional control
finding: High-anxiety people show worse attentional control. Deficit is in efficiency, not effectiveness; in inhibition and shifting but not updating; larger under high cognitive load. Age and anxiety severity moderate.
numbers: 58 studies, N=8292, Hedges g=-0.58 overall.
limits: Abstract only; per-subtype g not read. Preregistered (PROSPERO CRD42016036927). Mostly student samples.
agent_relevance: Supports ACT main predictions. No updating deficit means holding facts in context may survive pressure while switching and filtering do not. Load matters: put hard sub-tasks in their own short context.

source: Moran (2016) Anxiety and working memory capacity: a meta-analysis and narrative review
finding: Self-reported anxiety reliably goes with lower working-memory capacity. Similar across span types, largest for dynamic (n-back) tasks. Induced anxiety also hurts performance in the narrative review.
limits: Abstract read. Prior evidence was mixed; author lists methodological limits. Effect small to moderate and correlational.
agent_relevance: Updating-type load is hit hardest. Effect is modest, so do not over-engineer anxiety guards.

source: Hedge, Powell & Sumner (2018) The reliability paradox: why robust cognitive tasks do not produce reliable individual differences
finding: Robust Stroop and flanker effects are poor measures of individual differences. Difference scores are less reliable than their parts. Low reliability comes from small between-person variance, not noisy trials.
numbers: Test-retest ICC, 3 weeks apart. Flanker RT cost .40 (Study 1, N=47) and .57 (Study 2, N=57); Stroop RT cost .60 and .66; Stroop error cost .48/.44; SSRT .43 to .49. No measure above .8. Flanker RT cost vs Stroop RT cost r=.14 observed, .25 disattenuated. SSRT vs go/no-go commission rho=.52 observed, .90 disattenuated.
limits: Undergraduates; two studies; authors do not call tasks invalid, only unfit for ranking people. Disattenuation is an estimate.
agent_relevance: Any per-prompt switch cost or interference score for an agent needs many repeats; single-run deltas are noise.

source: Rey-Mermet, Gade & Oberauer (2018) Should we stop thinking about inhibition?
finding: Eleven inhibition tasks correlate only weakly with each other despite good single-task reliability. Two weak factors; low explanatory power; no general age deficit.
numbers: 11 tasks (antisaccade, stop-signal, colour and number Stroop, arrow and letter flanker, Simon, global-local, compatibility, n-2 repetition). Older adults worse at prepotent-response inhibition, better at distracter resistance.
limits: Abstract read. Sample sizes not read.
agent_relevance: Do not build one inhibition operator. Stroop-style and stop-style failures need different guards.

source: Response inhibition as a control process distinct from common executive function: two-study paper (J Exp Psychol Learn Mem Cogn, 2025; authors not recorded)
finding: Challenge to the inhibition = common EF reading: stop-style response inhibition forms a separate factor, once go/no-go or SART commission measures are included.
numbers: Study 1 N=154 exploratory; Study 2 N=279 confirmatory. Two-factor CFI .947, RMSEA .022 vs one-factor CFI .650, RMSEA .057; delta BIC -32.6. Factor correlation r=-.08.
limits: Not preregistered; some tasks have low split-half reliability (digit span .35); flanker loaded on nothing.
agent_relevance: Theory is unsettled. Keep stop-type and filter-type guards separate in the schema.

source: Gustavson et al. (2020) Lower general executive function is primarily associated with trait worry
finding: Worry, not anxiety symptoms, depression or rumination, goes with weak Common EF. Updating-Specific and Shifting-Specific are unrelated to all four.
numbers: N=192 students, 9 EF tasks. Worry-Common EF beta=-.43 (CI -.68 to -.17). Latent r with Common EF: anxiety -.07, depression -.14, rumination -.01.
limits: Correlational; unselected students; power only for r about .29 or larger. Cuts against a simple anxiety-hurts-shifting reading.
agent_relevance: The harmful ingredient may be worry-like content, not arousal. Avoid injecting self-referential threat text into agent context.

source: Attentional control in subclinical anxiety and depression (Frontiers in Psychology, 2020; authors not recorded)
finding: Failed ACT prediction: trait anxiety and depression did not predict worse distractor inhibition in a Posner task.
numbers: N=71 analysed. STAI-T: delta R2=.003, BF01=1.56. BDI-II: delta R2=.001, BF01=1.81. Depression did predict blocked target facilitation (delta R2=.096, p=.01).
limits: Bayes factors only anecdotal; subclinical sample; not a direct ACT test.
agent_relevance: Anxiety effects are task dependent; do not assume a universal filter failure.

source: Bukowski, Vaquero, Acosta & Lupianez (2026) Context-specific allocation of attentional control in anxiety and uncontrollability
finding: Anxious people learn context-control cues normally at first but fail to re-learn after the cue mapping flips. Points to flexibility loss, not a general control deficit.
numbers: Exp1 N=54 (24 high, 30 low trait anxiety). Re-learning CSPC effect: low anxiety 30 ms, high anxiety -4 ms; t(52)=-3.03, p=.004, d=-0.83. Exp2 N=74: uncontrollability 5 ms vs control 21 ms in learning phase, d=0.55.
limits: Exploratory re-learning effect; underpowered; dichotomised anxiety; control group also shrank in phase 2.
agent_relevance: Matches S6: an agent anchored to an old context rule needs a fresh context to re-learn after a rule flip.

source: Working memory training on test anxiety and attentional control in adolescents (BMC Psychology, 2024; authors not recorded)
finding: Dual n-back training lowered self-reported test anxiety but did not improve attentional control or flanker/go-nogo transfer versus an active control.
numbers: N=40 (21 training, 19 control), 10 sessions. Test anxiety group x time F(1,38)=5.15, p=.03, partial eta2=.12; post-test group difference p=.22. Attentional control scale p=.26. N-back level rose d=1.65 but control also gained d=1.07.
limits: Small, no follow-up, expectancy possible. Weak support for training fixes.
agent_relevance: Practice on one task does not transfer; do not expect warm-up drills to raise control.

source: Laban et al. (2025) LLMs Get Lost in Multi-Turn Conversation
finding: Fifteen LLMs drop sharply when a task arrives in pieces over turns. Most of the loss is unreliability, not lost ability. Models propose answers early and then over-rely on them. Reasoning models deteriorate the same way.
numbers: Average drop 39% across six tasks, 200,000+ simulated conversations; Fig 1: -35% with aptitude -15% and unreliability +112%. o3 and DeepSeek-R1 deteriorate similarly; their replies are 33% longer on average.
quote: make early assumptions to fill in for missing information, prematurely attempt to propose finalized solutions
limits: Underspecified sharded setup; simulated user LLM; temperature 1 default.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for fresh context (S6): one clean restatement of the full task beats a long multi-turn history.

source: Laban et al. (2025) mitigation tests: recap, snowball, temperature
finding: Restating earlier information helps only partly. Lower temperature helps full prompts but barely helps sharded ones.
numbers: SNOWBALL (repeat all prior shards each turn) recovers 15-20% of the FULL-to-SHARDED loss; RECAP does better but needs the last turn known. Temperature 1.0 to 0.0: unreliability drops 50-80% for FULL/CONCAT; sharded GPT-4o-mini no gain, GPT-4o 15-20%.
limits: Only GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini in mitigation runs.
agent_relevance: Rebuilding one consolidated prompt each stage is the cheap fix; a greedy setting does not cure drift.

source: Laban et al. (2025) reliability metrics
finding: Authors split performance into aptitude (90th percentile) and unreliability (gap between best and worst runs).
numbers: A90 and U1900 metrics; GPT-4o sharded unreliability 41.0, 43.8, 31.8 at three assistant temperatures.
limits: Single task family design.
agent_relevance: Measure our scaffold by spread across runs, not only the mean.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
finding: LLM analogue of flanker interference: one irrelevant sentence added to grade-school math cuts accuracy; most base problems are not solved consistently under distractors.
numbers: GSM-IC-4K: fewer than 30% of base problems solved consistently (macro accuracy); text-davinci-003 macro accuracy 0 on over-2-step problems with role-overlap distractors. COT micro 72.4.
quote: Large language models can be easily distracted by irrelevant context
limits: 2022 models only; arithmetic only; no current-model numbers.
agent_relevance: Test current models before trusting any guard; stripping irrelevant text in code is the surest lever.

source: Shi et al. (2023) instruction and exemplar effects
finding: An instruction to ignore irrelevant information helps; exemplars showing distractors help more without hurting original GSM8K.
numbers: COT micro 72.4 to 77.8 with instruction; 0-COT 29.0 to 30.5 (little change); LTM 77.5 to 80.6. COT macro 6.0 to 15.0 with instruction.
limits: Macro accuracy stays low; LTM worse than COT on macro for text-davinci-003.
agent_relevance: A cheap instruction gives small gains; filtering in code is stronger.

source: Deficient executive control in transformer attention (PNAS Nexus, 2026; authors not recorded)
finding: Vision LLMs fail a colour Stroop task as lists get long, with no sign of conflict adaptation. Interference grows with load.
numbers: GPT-4o incongruent accuracy 91% (5 words), 57% (10), 22% (20), 15% (40); congruent 99% at 20. Claude 3.5 Sonnet incongruent 76% at 20, 24% at 40. Word reading near 99%. Mixed lists: GPT-4o incongruent 1% at 20 and 40. Congruency sequence effect absent (Claude 10 words p=0.03, fails correction). GPT-5, Opus 4.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro (n=5 each) similar; Gemini incongruent 72%.
limits: Two main models, images not text, accuracy only, 30 trials per length, length confounded with colour repetition; supplement mitigations not read.
agent_relevance: Keep contexts short and clean; let code do word versus colour separation. GPT-5 thinking bypassed the task by writing code.

source: Xu, Verguts & Braem (2026) Cognitive flexibility versus stability via activation-based and weight-based adaptations
finding: Model of switch costs: fast trial-to-trial control state plus slow learned control settings. Training in a high-switch setting lowers switch cost; control is context-specific.
numbers: LSTM 32 units, 100 runs per study, 5 tasks, 90% vs 10% switch rate. Study 1 F(1,99)=77.39; Study 2 F(1,198)=1791.59. Human reanalysis N=102: switch cost difference -36.39 ms vs -8.11 ms, F=8.77, p=.004.
limits: Error rates only, not fitted to behaviour; small human reanalysis.
agent_relevance: Switch cost depends on expected switch rate; a fresh context per stage avoids misled carry-over control.

source: Coda-Forno et al. (2024) Inducing anxiety in large language models can induce bias
finding: Anxiety-inducing preprompts raise LLM anxiety scores and bias answers; more anxious prompt, more bias. But neutral preprompts also raised bias.
numbers: 12 LLMs tested; 6 passed consistency checks. Anxious vs neutral preprompt STICSA higher for all (t > 3.36, p < .01). Bias: anxious beta=0.62, p=.004; neutral beta=0.71, p=.001; STICSA beta=0.08, p=.02. GPT-4 and Claude-1 showed no positive link (less than half as biased).
limits: Preprompt length confound possible; two models contradict; questionnaire is a human instrument.
agent_relevance: Emotional text in context shifts outputs. Strip urgency text; a neutral preamble is not a safe control.

source: Ben-Zion et al. (2025) Assessing and alleviating state anxiety in large language models
finding: Traumatic narratives more than doubled GPT-4's state-anxiety score; relaxation text cut it only part way.
numbers: GPT-4 STAI-s baseline 30.8 (SD 3.96); after trauma 67.8 (SD 8.94); after relaxation 44.4 (SD 10.74), about 33% lower than trauma but about 50% above baseline.
limits: One model; five narratives and five relaxations; performance and bias not measured; anxiety is metaphor.
agent_relevance: A calming prompt does not restore baseline; a fresh context does.

source: Friedman & Miyake (2017): shifting versus common EF trade-off
finding: Heritability does not mean fixed. Shifting-Specific is the only factor with real environment variance, and it trades off with Common EF in toddlers.
numbers: Shifting-Specific 21% environmental variance; better self-restraint toddlers had better Common EF but worse Shifting-Specific.
limits: Review text; no training trial.
agent_relevance: Tight goal maintenance and easy switching may pull against each other; one knob will not tune both.

source: Search gap note: no large preregistered ACT replication found (Europe PMC title searches)
finding: Title searches found one preregistered meta-analysis (Shi 2019) and several small 2020-2026 studies, but no large multi-site replication of ACT.
numbers: Small studies seen: N=71, N=54, N=74, N=40.
limits: Not a systematic search; WebSearch budget was exhausted, so this is absence from a limited search.
agent_relevance: Treat ACT-derived agent design as a hypothesis; test on our own harness.

source: Hedge, Powell & Sumner (2018) go/no-go and stop-signal reliability
finding: Stop-type tasks are less reliable than Stroop cost; go/no-go commission errors are among the best measures.
numbers: Go/No-go commission ICC .76 in both studies; omission .69/.42; stop-signal go RT .35/.57; SSRT integration .36/.49.
limits: Undergraduates, 3-week gap.
agent_relevance: Count-based error measures (commission errors) are steadier than timing deltas; prefer counted checks (G5).

source: Coda-Forno et al. (2024) model differences
finding: Anxiety induction worked only on RLHF-tuned models; the two non-RLHF models (GPT-3, Falcon-40b-instruct) were already high at baseline and did not shift.
limits: Only six models passed the consistency screen; older models.
agent_relevance: Susceptibility to emotional framing is model-specific; check it on our chosen model before adding any guard.
